title: Reload an open scene when a base further up the chain changes
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Part of #7984 (open since 2016)

These reports describe an open scene that does not follow a base scene after a save, and they need this editor side:

> #28090, #10156, #86876

I rebuilt #28090 in 4.8 and measured it against a stock build. It fails on stock and passes here. That case adds and deletes nodes rather than properties. I did not rebuild #10156 or #86876. They describe the same symptom, so I expect this change to help them, but I did not measure that. The companion PR, #124022, lists a larger group for the base state side, and I measured three of those. Two more reports, #55964 and #56584, describe the same symptom, and both closed as archived rather than fixed. They are worth a re-test after this.

One report in this area needs a different change, and these pull requests do not give it. #84759 asks for an open scene to follow a base that Save All Scenes writes while the reader sits on that same tab. The check runs when a scene tab becomes current, so a save from the tab itself never reaches it. Both builds behave the same way there. The save path would have to run the same check, and that is a separate change.

Some reports about scripts and exported variables (#53766, #46103, #92879, #44526, #90418) look like the same base state mechanism, and nobody measured that. Reports about `local_to_scene` resources (#94531, #94919) look like a separate defect in resource identity, and neither PR addresses them.

`EditorData::_find_updated_instances()` asks each node for the scene it came from, and it compares that one file's modification time. A node only exposes the scene it came from directly. A base further up a chain contributes no node, so the editor never looked at it.

```
Base.tscn     edited and saved
   ^ inherits
Middle.tscn   no node in the open tree -- never checked
   ^ instanced
Outer.tscn    open in the editor, still shows the old base
```

The open scene keeps the stale base until you close it and open it again. A scene that sits directly on that base refreshes correctly. That difference is what makes the defect look intermittent.

PR #107913 is an open attempt at the same issue. Its author identified the problem, and writes that the scene refreshes once and then needs a manual reload. This PR pairs with the base state fix in #124022 to address that follow-on staleness. A regression test drives repeated base saves. A single save cannot separate a good refresh from a stored override.

## Additional information

**This is the second of two PRs. It must merge after the base scene state fix** (#124022, in `scene/resources/packed_scene.{cpp,h}`). Detection here compares a scene file's modification time against the time recorded in the state derived from it. While `get_base_scene_state()` reached through to the live base, that recorded time moved with every save, so the comparison could never differ. The snapshot in the first PR is what makes detection possible. That commit sits beneath this branch, so this diff contains it until the first PR merges.

A helper now walks each scene state up its chain of base scenes and looks at every file. The walk notes each state it saw, not each path. Two branches of one tree can hold separate snapshots of the same base file, taken either side of a save. A path would therefore let the current branch stand in for the stale one. Noting states also keeps the walk finite if a chain comes back on itself. The helper reads each file once per pass into a small cache.

For reviewers: this adds `tests/editor/`, which does not exist upstream today. The build stays as it is. `test_main.cpp` already handles the `[Editor]` tag, and `tests/SCsub` globs recursively. `_find_updated_instances()` is private, and the test reaches it through a friend accessor, one added line in `editor_data.h`. `ProjectSettings` uses the same arrangement for `TestProjectSettingsInternalsAccessor`. If the maintainers do not want an editor test directory, the tests can go, and neither fix changes. The friend declaration goes with them.

Coverage: the four nesting shapes, a chain of four with each level edited in turn, and alternating inheriting and instancing. Also one base shared by two branches, two branches that hold different snapshots of one base, and a case with no save at all. A second test file carries detection through the reload itself. It asserts over repeated base saves that the reloaded scene still follows the base and stores no override of its own.

**AI use:** I developed this change with AI assistance (Claude) for investigation, implementation and test authoring. I reviewed all of it. I drove the behavior by hand in the editor over three rounds of base saves. I also ran the full automated suite (1438 cases, 424492 assertions, passing).
